title: E-commerce order where only the second line item carries a discount
rationale: Optional per-row fields are unavoidable in real order data. flattenList collects field vectors by appending as it encounters each element and then pads with nulls at the END, so a field absent from earlier elements has its values shifted to the front. This produces a silently wrong money value on the wrong row.
catchesBugClass: Positional misalignment in the columnar transposition of heterogeneous object arrays; absent-key versus present-null conflation inside array elements.
cannotCatch: It cannot detect the symmetric case where the sparse field is absent from the LAST element instead of the first; that one pads correctly by luck and would pass.

predicted.detail: THE MIGRATION IS FIXED IN 2.1.0; THE FABRICATED NULL IS NOT. discount_pct now stays on line item 2 (SKU-205) where the document put it - previously it was applied to line item 1 (SKU-100), silent financial corruption that round-tripped with a correct field count and a plausible shape. What keeps this row DEFECT is that line item 1 still gains an explicit discount_pct of null that it never carried. A consumer cannot tell 'no discount was recorded' from 'a discount of null was recorded'.
